macro_themes.title: Geopolitical Escalation & Safe-Haven Demand
macro_themes.summary: Renewed escalation in the Middle East has triggered a significant flight to safety, driving demand for traditional safe-haven assets. Gold has spiked to near all-time highs ($2380.50), while the US Dollar (DXY 106.15) and Japanese Yen (USD/JPY 158.98) are also benefiting. This risk-off sentiment is broadly weighing on risk-sensitive currencies like AUD and NZD, and commodity-linked CAD. The immediate focus is on de-escalation efforts, but market participants remain highly sensitive to any further negative headlines.

macro_themes.title: Fed 'Higher for Longer' Narrative Solidifies
macro_themes.summary: Stronger-than-expected US inflation data and hawkish commentary from several Fed officials have reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain higher interest rates for an extended period. The US 10-year Treasury yield has climbed to 4.65%, widening yield differentials against most G10 peers. This divergence in monetary policy expectations is a key driver of USD strength, particularly against currencies whose central banks are perceived to be closer to cutting rates, such as the EUR and GBP.

macro_themes.title: JPY Intervention Watch Intensifies
macro_themes.summary: The Japanese Yen continues its relentless depreciation, with USD/JPY now trading at 158.98, pushing closer to the 160.00 level widely considered a red line for intervention by Japanese authorities. Verbal warnings from Finance Minister Suzuki and BOJ Governor Ueda have increased in frequency and intensity. While no direct intervention has occurred yet, the market remains on high alert, with any significant move above current levels likely to trigger action. This risk creates volatility and uncertainty for JPY crosses.

macro_themes.title: ECB Dovish Tilt vs. Sticky Eurozone Inflation
macro_themes.summary: Despite persistent, albeit moderating, inflation in the Eurozone, the European Central Bank appears increasingly inclined towards a rate cut in June, driven by concerns over economic growth. Recent comments from ECB officials suggest a dovish bias, contrasting with the more hawkish stance of the Fed. This policy divergence is exerting downward pressure on the Euro, with EUR/USD trading at 1.1782, as investors price in earlier and potentially more aggressive rate cuts from the ECB compared to the Fed.

macro_themes.title: BoE's Inflation Dilemma & Growth Concerns
macro_themes.summary: The Bank of England faces a challenging balancing act as UK inflation remains stubbornly high, yet economic growth shows signs of fragility. While headline CPI has eased, core inflation components are proving sticky, making the BoE hesitant to commit to early rate cuts. However, the broader global risk-off environment and a strong USD are weighing on GBP. GBP/USD is trading at 1.3544, vulnerable to both domestic economic data and shifts in global risk sentiment.
